newsitem.title: USA: TI semiconductor revs fuel strong Q2.
newsitem.headline: TI semiconductor revs fuel strong Q2.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said Tuesday that strong semiconductor revenues, especially from its digital signal processors, and higher operating margins fueled better-than-expected second quarter earnings.
The Dallas-based semiconductor giant said semiconductor revenues in the quarter rose 17 percent from a year earlier and 10 percent from the first quarter.
Operating profits from semiconductors were up fourfold from a year ago and up 45 percent from the first quarter, it said.
TI's second quarter net income from continuing operations was $213 million, up from $41 million a year ago.
Net earnings per share were $1.07, up from $0.21 a year earlier. According to First Call, industry analysts had expected earnings of around $0.87 per share.
Revenues rose 7 percent, to $2.56 billion from $2.4 billion a year ago.

"This was a very good quarter," President and Chief Executive Officer Thomas Engibous said in a statement. "We realize the opportunity for TI is significant, especially as digital signal processing becomes the core element in a growing number of electronic products."
Digital signal processors (DSPs), which are primarily used in the audio and video functions of electronic equipment, lie at the core of TI's new strategy.

With the recent sale of its defense, notebook and software divisions, semiconductors now account for 80 percent of the company's revenues, and fast-growing DSPs make up more than 40 percent of semiconductor sales, the company said.
"We are moving quickly and aggressively to extend our leadership in this rapidly growing market," Engibous said.
Last year's second quarter results were battered by a sharp decline in prices for DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chips.
TI said its DRAM losses continued to narrow in the 1997 second quarter, but pricing pressures increased toward the end of the period. The market will remain volatile in the near-term, it said.

Despite the problems with DRAMs, second quarter semiconductor orders rose 72 percent from a year ago. It said semiconductor orders, excluding memory chips, were also up from the first quarter, but it gave no details.

"TI's outlook for longer-term semiconductor market growth remains positive, and plans for 1997 continue to be based on a moderate market recovery," the company said. "As a result, TI expects capital expenditures in 1997 to be at or slightly above the previous forecast of $1.1 billion."
The operating margin in the semiconductor division rose 10 percentage points from the year-ago period, and rose four percentage points from the first quarter.
Overall operating margin, excluding special charges, rose to 13 percent from 2 percent a year earlier.

Revenues and profits from operations in TI's materials and controls business rose 5 percent and 46 percent, respectively, to record levels, in part because of increased demand for radio frequency identification systems. Operating profit margins are at double-digit levels.
Second quarter calculator revenues were up 19 percent from the same period last year.
